composition.observation: The camera/target instrument dominates desktop, with instruction and recognition beside it; phone stacks these into one continuous workspace. Prepare, calibration, check and practice keep the same sea-green frame and restrained brass emphasis.

hierarchy.observation: Find your point leads to Meet your hand, followed by a named stage and one principal action. Training completion explicitly asks for five new targets before the result, so readiness and independent accuracy are not presented as the same milestone.

typography.observation: Large serif task headings and ordinary sans-serif instructions remain readable at original resolution. Small technical metrics stay subordinate to the session result, and mobile results retain the demo/experimental qualifier rather than hiding it in an unrelated screen.

spacing.observation: The desktop target has useful clear area and instructions have separate groups. The phone leaves adequate separation around pause, retry and target controls; vertical scrolling is necessary but does not force simultaneous precision in two cramped columns.

controls.observation: Pause changes to Resume without discarding completed targets; subsequent targets, the five-point check, practice target and tracking-condition selector all cause visibly different outcomes. Retry live camera and Explore guided demo are clear conventional alternatives.

contrast.observation: Main instructions use pale text on deep green, while principal buttons and target outlines use brass. Focus rings and the independent-check mark are plainly distinguishable. The result is readable at native resolution; this visual observation is supplemented by the captured serious/critical accessibility checks.

consistency.observation: Typography, green surfaces, brass task emphasis and the home/account shell belong to the accepted Homeport family. The instrument changes its working plane between setup and calibration while retaining the same return control and stage vocabulary.

states.observation: Welcome, camera failure, disclosed simulated tracking, training, pause, required independent check, validation, result and playground all render. Detection count, framing/posture and eligibility remain separate observations; the two-hand scenario does not falsely become two simultaneous input cursors.

responsive.observation: Mobile preparation puts camera preview first; calibration scrolls the active target and controls into view. Desktop preserves side-by-side target and recognition. The original mobile controls remain legible and the capture reports no horizontal overflow in its declared states.

keyboard.observation: The full captured target/check/recovery journeys use Tab reachability and Enter activation for the named actions, with native selector keys for the demo condition. Traces and visible gold focus support these specific conventional paths; no physical assistive-technology test is claimed.

focus.observation: Welcome heading, active target plane, Resume and the demo-condition combobox show visible focus at the appropriate step. The return reaches the device-connection task. Focus is observed through screenshots and the captured keyboard sequence, rather than inferred solely from accessible labels.

feedback.observation: Guidance changes between Move the demo hand, collecting, paused, Independent check required and passed. Original software feedback measurements range about 840–899 ms for the selected boundaries, comfortably within the five-second contract; they exclude actual camera latency and inference accuracy.

motion.observation: Normal recordings show a moving simulated hand/target and settling feedback; reduced recordings preserve the same controls and independent result with a restrained presentation. Complete chronological diagnostic inspection found no persistent blank working state. The 2fps survey is not frame-time instrumentation.

continuity.observation: Setup, calibration, check and practice remain in the Reach workspace and the visible Device connections return restores its origin. The unchanged home-link continuity digest supports the observed return; this laboratory does not activate a Voyage target or move progression authority.

complexity.observation: A four-stage progress strip, contextual instructions and one main action make the instrument comprehensible. Absolute pointing is explicitly experimental and relative movement is separately offered; session diagnostics and demo controls are disclosed instead of dominating the initial task.

role-outcomes.observation: The declared anonymous laboratory journey actually progresses through nine training targets and five new validation targets, reaches practice, and distinguishes detected/ineligible tracking. Relative control has its own setup and result. These are disclosed demo outcomes, not evidence of real-person webcam accuracy.

fallbacks.observation: A failed live-camera start gives Retry live camera and Explore guided demo; the demo remains plainly labeled CAMERA OFF and explains its physical-proof limit. Conventional navigation and safe return remain usable after failure and after a completed demo.

composition.observation: The released spatial clue opens as a distinct focused dialog over the Journal, with Voyage identity, Guided View explanation, parchment clue and contextual actions. On phone the dialog fits a deliberate single-column composition rather than repeating the book spread.

hierarchy.observation: A message between worlds and Guided View establish purpose before the Captain’s note and Inspect controls. The original clue remains the focal content; capability explanation and the recorded-interaction message follow it instead of displacing it.

typography.observation: The actual clue and its Inspect result are readable in the native mobile captures. Serif clue headings, clear body text and a smaller capability explanation give the dialog a recognizable reading hierarchy, consistent with parchment content elsewhere in the Voyage.

spacing.observation: The phone gives the clue a substantial parchment area, wraps actions into two understandable rows, and separates the lower capability/status section. Desktop keeps a bounded dialog rather than spreading the short clue across the entire viewport.

controls.observation: Open Chronicle Lens presents the released note; Inspect changes the visible article to You are inspecting the Captain’s note. Close Chronicle Lens returns to Journal tools at the same route. These are actual consumer actions, not just a role heading.

contrast.observation: Dark ink on parchment makes the clue legible; pale text on the blue-green dialog and gold/teal focus rings distinguish the controls. The original images retain clear separation between content, actions and secondary capability text.

consistency.observation: The compass motif, green shell, parchment clue, brass emphasis and restrained dialog match the accepted Homeport family. Lens remains visually distinct from the Journal while carrying the same recognizable Voyage identity.

states.observation: Journal-ready, Lens-ready, inspected and returned states all render with meaningful text. The result records an inspection and tells the player to continue through the passage when ready, without implying that inspection itself progressed the Voyage.

responsive.observation: The 390px phone dialog retains Close, Choose, Inspect and Place in Guided View without clipping the clue horizontally. The desktop keeps the same task order in a wider bounded surface. Returned mobile Journal content is scrollable with the Lens entry visible.

keyboard.observation: Captured visible-control journeys reach Open Lens, Inspect and Close by Tab and activate with Enter; the traces corroborate the changing rendered outcomes. This establishes the named keyboard path, with no claim of a complete screen-reader or switch-device assessment.

focus.observation: A clear gold ring identifies the Lens Close control on entry and the Open Chronicle Lens trigger after return. Inspect produces its visible result inside the same dialog. Focus stays understandable against the dimmed Journal.

feedback.observation: Inspect produces the concrete note description and Interaction recorded message. Captured activation-to-outcome maxima are approximately 209–516 ms across desktop/phone normal/reduced cases; these software measurements support the observed prompt response and do not measure hardware AR.

motion.observation: Normal and reduced recordings preserve a stable clue during modal arrival, inspection and return. The complete sequences show a useful readable destination after loading, and reduced motion preserves hierarchy and actions. The visible Journal fallback notices are retained as a limit to any broad cinematic-smoothness claim.

continuity.observation: The dialog opens and closes within the same published Journal route and retains its Voyage title. Original continuity observations bind both Voyage and edition before, at outcomes and after return; no new identity or progression system is substituted.

complexity.observation: A single contextual Open Lens entry reaches the actual clue, followed by direct Inspect and Close controls. No account administration or technical role selection is needed for this published-clue journey; Guided View capability explanation is placed beside the experience.

role-outcomes.observation: The player receives a recognizable Lens with the actual authored northern-light clue and a real Inspect response. This is a canonical Guided spatial consumer, not the duplicate Journal failure described in the objective. Native camera/world tracking is not established by the browser evidence.

fallbacks.observation: The dialog explicitly uses Guided View and calls it readable, seated and camera-free. The same released clue survives that tier and Close returns to the Journal. No simulated camera capability is marketed as true world-tracked AR.

composition.observation: Connect is a quiet control beside the active Voyage, and the focused Bring your phone aboard dialog keeps the live book recognizable behind it. Scan-first QR, optional code and a direct Chronicle return form one clear task.

hierarchy.observation: The pairing dialog leads with the current Voyage and scan instruction, then same-account guidance and a short-lived code alternative. Connected confirmation replaces the QR rather than leaving obsolete credentials beside success. The book remains the primary desktop task.

typography.observation: Pairing titles, scan instructions, connected-device names and pending/received messages are readable at original resolution. Small status text remains subordinate; mobile Journal chrome is more crowded than the dedicated companion, recorded as minor polish.

spacing.observation: Pairing and send dialogs use bounded grouped controls, with generous QR separation and clear return. Dedicated phone companions have usable padding. The returned phone Journal allocates excessive vertical space to navigation/replay controls, but scrolling and its persistent Continue action remain available.

controls.observation: Actual second-context Join, purpose changes, Send view, Receive, Cancel send, Decline and Recover all have meaningful rendered outcomes. Ordinary pairing stays inside the Chronicle; advanced transfer participation is disclosed under More ways to open.

contrast.observation: The green/brass dialogs, legible ink content, clear QR and visible focus rings remain recognizable against the dimmed book. State distinctions are expressed in text as well as colored dots, including Offline and Reconnect this device.

consistency.observation: Desktop book, focused phone connection, dedicated companion and recovery share the same Voyagewright visual family and task vocabulary. Same Voyage identity follows the crossing rather than exposing session or surface identifiers to ordinary controls.

states.observation: Normal/reduced paired media cover connect, same-Voyage join, pending offer, rendered receipt, offline, reconnect and recovery. Adverse media show cancelled/expired-code refusal, private confirmation, sender cancel, receiver decline, restricted crew content and removal of a revoked private view.

responsive.observation: Phone pairing is scan/code-oriented; the actual 390px companions are readable and the 844px landscape and 820px medium views retain contextual controls without horizontal overflow. The ordinary Journal return header is tall and merits polish, while the real Continue control stays visible and executable.

keyboard.observation: Generic contextual connect/return journeys demonstrate Tab reachability and Enter activation, with visible trigger focus. Paired form Join also works with Enter, and Escape cancels pairing. Paired phone contexts have isMobile/hasTouch enabled; physical touch and assistive-device behavior remain untested.

focus.observation: Closing pairing restores focus to Connect another device, visible in generic captured returns and explicitly checked in paired tests. Native dialogs retain a clear active control. The adverse Escape path returns safely to the existing book rather than stranding focus in a removed overlay.

feedback.observation: Sender ready-to-receive precedes receiver acceptance; is open on your other device follows actual content presentation. Original paired timings are QR 492/576 ms, join 513/932 ms, offer 512/786 ms and acceptance-to-rendered receipt 475/849 ms for normal/reduced, excluding physical latency.

motion.observation: Complete recordings preserve the book during pairing and replace companion purposes with useful content. Short source-cadence frame sequences show bounded settling without a persistent blank destination. Reduced motion keeps equivalent outcomes. Animation fallback notices and post-outage SSE 429/retry observations limit any claim of flawless cinema or frame pacing.

continuity.observation: Separate desktop/phone contexts share the original witness Voyage and edition but have distinct authorized surfaces. Continue Voyage performs the canonical progression request; Return to Current Objective reveals the new Voyage complete leaf while desktop can retain a remembered reading position. Route return alone is not treated as progression proof.

complexity.observation: Ordinary joining starts with one Chronicle control, scan/code guidance and a Join action after account authorization. It avoids Personal Harbor. Purpose switching and manual transfer use plain names; advanced transfer modes remain disclosed rather than presenting a distributed-system questionnaire.

role-outcomes.observation: The real paired phone changes from full Journal text to actual Guided Lens, authored Chart/objective, compass artifact, letter and restricted crew content. A role label is not used as completion evidence. Prepared canonical synthetic sessions establish authorization for these paired joins; a full phone password roundtrip is not captured.
